_quarry.description: Wheeled plough with a coulter, iron share, and mouldboard that turned the dense, wet soils of northern Europe in a way the Mediterranean scratch-plough could not. Adoption was slow and uneven through the eighth and ninth centuries but was widespread by the year 1000. With the three-field rotation and the horse collar it underpinned the agricultural surplus that fed the eleventh- and twelfth-century European expansion.
